steps.title: Analyse the problem
steps.description:
We must evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^{π/8} x sin(2x) dx. 
Givens: • integrand x sin(2x) • limits 0 to π/8.
Relevant topics from the curriculum:
1. Integration—Continued: “find integrals using integration by parts” (main tool).
2. Functions and Differentiation: knowledge of basic derivatives of trigonometric functions (needed to compute antiderivative of sin(2x)).
3. One-variable optimisation/curve-sketching skills are not directly required here, but understanding of definite integrals as areas reinforces why limits are applied.
steps.hints: Identify which factor to differentiate and which to integrate to apply integration by parts efficiently.

steps.title: Choose u and dv for integration by parts
steps.description: Let u = x (easy to differentiate), dv = sin(2x) dx (easy to integrate).

steps.title: Compute v and du
steps.description:
du = dx.
Integral of sin(2x) is −cos(2x)/2, so v = −½ cos(2x).
steps.hints: Differentiate u; integrate dv using the standard derivative d/dx[cos(2x)] = −2 sin(2x).

steps.title: Apply integration by parts and evaluate the remaining integral
steps.description:
∫₀^{π/8} x sin(2x) dx = [x(−½ cos(2x))]₀^{π/8} − ∫₀^{π/8}(−½ cos(2x)) dx
= −½ x cos(2x) |₀^{π/8} + ½ ∫₀^{π/8} cos(2x) dx.
steps.hints: Keep the ½ factor outside to simplify algebra.

steps.title: Compute the boundary term
steps.description:
At x = π/8: −½(π/8)cos(π/4) = −(π/8)(√2/4) = −π√2/32.
At x = 0: term is 0.
Boundary contribution = −π√2/32.
steps.hints: cos(π/4)=√2/2; remember cos(0)=1 but it is multiplied by x=0.

steps.title: Integrate cos(2x) and evaluate
steps.description:
∫ cos(2x) dx = ½ sin(2x).
So ½ ∫₀^{π/8} cos(2x) dx = ½[½ sin(2x)]₀^{π/8} = ¼ sin(π/4) = ¼(√2/2) = √2/8.
